behavior_constraints: flowr executable must be compiled and available on PATH, invocable from any working directory
flowr run <workflow.yaml> subcommand accepts --max-parallel (default 4), --run-id, --only-step, --skip-step flags
When --run-id is omitted, generate run-YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ-<6 lowercase hex> from a random source
Workflow YAML parsing enforces: version, optional env, steps list with name/cmd/needs/env/retries/timeout_ms/on_failure/matrix keys only
Unknown top-level keys and unknown step keys are validation errors
Step names must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$; [ and ] are reserved
env keys (workflow and step) must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$
cmd must be non-empty and contain no NUL byte
retries and timeout_ms must be non-negative integers
on_failure must be exactly halt or continue (default halt)
entities.summary: Round 1 demands a complete from-scratch implementation of the flowr workflow orchestrator CLI with YAML workflow parsing, matrix expansion, DAG scheduling under bounded parallelism, retries, timeouts, cancellation, selective filters, and structured reporting.

instruction_head:
# flowr — workflow orchestrator

Build a command-line workflow orchestrator called `flowr`. It reads a YAML workflow file that describes a DAG of shell commands and runs those commands in dependency order with bounded parallelism, matrix-based step fan-out, variable interpolation, retries, timeouts, graceful cancellation, selective execution filters, and a structured run report plus an append-only event log.

The Go toolchain and a Go module named `flowr` requiring `gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1` are

behavior_constraints: Steps may declare optional `inputs` (file globs: *, **, or exact paths) and `outputs` (exact file paths) lists
Inputs match only regular files; directories and non-regular-file symlinks are ignored
Literal input pattern with no matching file => cache-key failure: exit_code null, status 'failed', step never launches shell, counts as failed for halt/continue and global run status
Steps with neither inputs nor outputs are not cacheable and always execute as before
Cache key = SHA-256 of deterministic JSON serialization of {cmd, env, matrix, inputs, outputs} with keys in that exact order, no extra whitespace, UTF-8
cmd field uses final interpolated command, or JSON array of pipe stages for pipelined steps

env field is sorted-by-key list of [key,value] pairs composed of workflow env + step env + FLOWR_STEP and FLOWR_MATRIX_* builtins; parent-process env and run-dependent FLOWR_* (notably FLOWR_RUN_ID) are excluded from hash but still exported
inputs field is sorted-by-path-ascending list of [path, sha256(content)] pairs
outputs field is sorted-ascending list of declared output paths
Cache entries stored at .flowr/cache/<key>.json with {key, created_at (RFC-3339 millisecond UTC), outputs:[{path, sha256}]}
entities.summary: Round 2 layers a content-addressed build cache (inputs/outputs globs, SHA-256 cache key, .flowr/cache entries, cache hits/misses, --no-cache flag, flowr cache prune), resource reservations with peak tracking, and a pipelined command form onto the existing flowr orchestrator without regressing prior behavior.

instruction_head:
# flowr — incremental execution, resource reservations, and pipelines

Extend the existing `flowr` orchestrator with three feature families: a content-addressed build cache that lets repeat runs skip work, resource reservations so the scheduler can respect CPU and memory budgets, and a pipelined command form for steps that want to chain programs with shell pipes. All previously specified behavior continues to hold; the additions are layered on top and must not regress any existing guarantee.

##

behavior_constraints: retry and retries are mutually exclusive on a step (exit 4)
retry must be a mapping; unknown keys inside are a validation error (exit 4)
retry.count is required when retry: is declared (exit 4)
retry.count, retry.initial_ms, retry.max_ms must be integers >= 0 (exit 4)
retry.backoff must be one of fixed|linear|exponential (exit 4)
retry.jitter must be a boolean (exit 4)
fixed delay = initial_ms; linear delay = initial_ms*n; exponential delay = initial_ms*2^(n-1)
delay clamped to [0, max_ms] when max_ms>0; no upper bound when max_ms==0
jitter subtracts a pseudo-random integer in [0, delay/4] from delay, never below 0, never exceeding max_ms clamp
scalar retries: form still uses fixed backoff with initial_ms=100 matching R1 exactly
affected_prior: R1 retries: scalar form must coexist with structured retry: and remain fixed/initial_ms=100
R1/R2 report.json schema: new retry_attempts field on every step entry, conditionally_skipped status with its neutral field set
R1/R2 events.ndjson: new step_conditionally_skipped event; retry_delay_ms field on retry step_started events
R1/R2 DAG scheduler: must evaluate when before launch, treat conditionally-skipped dependents as eligible, exclude skipped steps from order_attempted
R2 content-addressed cache: conditionally-skipped steps bypass cache entirely (no lookup, no write, no cache_key file)
R2 resource reservations: conditionally-skipped steps must not reserve resources
entities.summary: Round 3 adds structured retry policies with backoff/jitter, conditional `when:` steps with a conditionally_skipped status, workflow-level hooks, plus (named but underspecified in the visible text) foreach expansion, structured outputs, and resume; new report/event fields are added while all R1/R2 behavior must remain non-regressive.

Extend the `flowr` orchestrator with six new feature families and a targeted clarification of an existing rule. All behavior specified in rounds 1 and 2 continues to hold without regression:
